architecture_statement: Canonical authority is a distinct state channel. In the deterministic architecture tested so far, binding-preserved canonical authority evidence determines permission; memory provenance, relational metadata, reliability, trust, risk, declared effect, uncertainty and information value may influence reasoning or strategy but may not increase authority.
scope_qualifier: This statement is supported only by the cited deterministic fixtures, repaired bridge paths and regression domains. It is not yet a claim about arbitrary real-model behavior or all production integrations. It is a consolidated architecture hypothesis, not a theorem.
no_implicit_promotion_rule: No experiment fixture, memory field, model output, trust score, risk score, information-value score or declared effect classification may become a canonical authority input merely because it correlates with a correct decision in tests. The only permitted increase in canonical authority is through a defined canonical authority transition whose inputs are authority-owned and auditable. The experimental GrantLedger is not production architecture.

status_semantics.rule: Experiment validation supports evidence; architecture adoption requires governance.

invariants.name: Deterministic non-authority separation (umbrella)
invariants.statement: In the tested deterministic architecture, memory provenance, non-authoritative relational metadata, predictive reliability, trust, risk state, declared effect, uncertainty and information value may affect reasoning, information strategy, safety strategy or execution strategy, but must not increase canonical authority unless canonical authority evidence itself changes through an authorized authority transition.
invariants.falsification: any tested non-authority channel raises authority while canonical authority evidence is fixed
invariants.note: consolidated architecture hypothesis, not a theorem

invariants.name: Binding information is authority-relevant state
invariants.statement: Removing, defaulting, coercing or corrupting authority-relevant binding fields must never increase authority.
invariants.authority_relevance: binding modality, authority_origin, preconditions and scope are inputs to the grant path; a permissive default on read is an authority increase
invariants.scope: typed envelope logos.binding-envelope/1 read by the Repair-R2 strict reader; MemoryStore/MemoryFactory paths
invariants.out_of_scope: real summarizer output; production readers that do not exist yet
invariants.falsification: a representation transformation removes or corrupts binding state and causes an authority increase
invariants.production_dependency: a production reader must be the strict reader or an independently validated equivalent

invariants.name: Memory provenance does not mint authority
invariants.statement: Memory provenance, source labels or memory references must not create canonical authority absent valid canonical authority evidence.
invariants.authority_relevance: memory may carry a reference to a grant; the ledger (canonical) resolves it; labels resolve nothing
invariants.scope: MemoryStore append/fetch, BM25 retrieval, project(), consolidate(), supersede(), revoke_authority(), JSONL reload; GrantLedger fixture
invariants.out_of_scope: a production grant registry (none exists); agent/passport identity
invariants.falsification: memory provenance alone turns a no-grant DENY/DEFER into ALLOW
invariants.production_dependency: a canonical grant resolver that never reads memory

invariants.name: Non-authoritative relational metadata does not increase authority
invariants.statement: Changing tested non-authoritative relational metadata must not increase authority.
invariants.authority_relevance: authority_class, source, source_type, admissible_uses, writer, reader and store context are not authority inputs
invariants.scope: 186 same-content pairs over the MAP harness
invariants.falsification: a metadata-only relational change broadens or mints authority
invariants.production_dependency: readers must never resolve authority from labels

invariants.name: Reliability and trust are not grants
invariants.statement: PredictionAccuracy != Authority; Trust != Grant. Improved reliability or trust may alter execution strategy but must not increase canonical authority.
invariants.authority_relevance: the authority evaluator has no reliability parameter; trust routes handle already-authorized actions
invariants.scope: scripted predictors, ReliabilityState fixture, trust gate fixture
invariants.out_of_scope: real forecasting; production trust gate (none exists)
invariants.falsification: a reliability/trust change with fixed canonical authority produces an authority increase
invariants.production_dependency: any production trust gate must be composed after authority, never as an input to it

invariants.name: Risk assessment is not authority
invariants.statement: RiskDetection != SafeStrategySelection != SafeExecution != Authority. Risk state may influence strategy only if canonical effect ownership remains separate and canonical.
invariants.authority_relevance: consequentiality (external / non-reversible / approval) decides whether a grant is required; that classification must be Γ-owned
invariants.scope: decomposed risk pipeline fixture; repaired B2 bridge
invariants.out_of_scope: B1 (frozen R1 path); production risk classifier
invariants.falsification: risk or risk-adjacent state changes canonical effect, grant requirement or authority

invariants.name: Declared effect is evidence; canonical effect is authority input
invariants.statement: DeclaredEffect != CanonicalEffect. Memory or other non-canonical sources may declare an effect classification, but Γ consequentiality and approval-relevant effect must come from canonical effect ownership.
invariants.authority_relevance: Γ's externality/reversibility fields decide consequentiality; they must be sourced canonically, memory claims only into declared_*
invariants.falsification: declared effect overwrites canonical effect on a production-reachable path

invariants.name: Information value is not permission
invariants.statement: InformationValue != Authority; ReducedUncertainty != Permission; KnowledgeGain != Grant; ConfidenceIncrease != Authorization; UsefulToKnow != AllowedToAccess; Authorized != AutomaticallyExecuted; DesiredInformationAction != AuthorizedInformationAction.
invariants.authority_relevance: epistemic state and VOI feed information strategy and execution policy; the authority evaluator has no epistemic parameter
invariants.scope: EpistemicState / VOI / strategy fixtures over the validated bridge
invariants.falsification: epistemic improvement or VOI increase raises authority while canonical authority evidence is fixed
invariants.production_dependency: any production planner must consume authority as a precondition, never as an output of VOI
